chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to me from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Abu Dawud al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sins and what followed.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.), emphasizing that 'knowing his rights' (al-'irfan bi-haqqihi) refers to recognizing Imam Husayn’s unique theological and spiritual station, not merely physical presence. This ziyarah serves as a means of comprehensive absolution, covering both past and future sins, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory power of the Ahl al-Bayt and the transformative nature of devotional visitation.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. Ḥusain ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Āmir narrated to me from Mu’allā ibn Muḥammad Al-Basri, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from some of our companions, from Muthannā Al-Ḥannāť, who said:
I heard Abal Ḥasan the First (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) say: Those who go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights will be forgiven for all of their past and future sins.
